then.message: You ate the last of your food over the weekend. Restock before next weekend.

else.message: There was no food at home. You spent the weekend hungry and feel weak.

then.message: You were evicted for unpaid rent! Back to your parents' place.
A note from the landlady: your rent is overdue.

do.message: Mom tidied your room again. Your things are 'somewhere safe'.
Dad left a printout of flat listings on your pillow.
Mom asked, loudly, when the neighbour's boy moved out. Age nineteen, apparently.

then.message: You have nothing decent to wear.
Too much work and too little rest: you feel worn out. Rest at home or go to the sauna.

setWorld.economy: clamp(world.economy + (rnd() - 0.5) * params.economyVolatility + (1 - world.economy) * params.economyPull, params.economyMin, params.economyMax)

lessonRequires.message: Your head is full. No more lessons this week.

turnEndChecks.message: There is no food at home. You will go hungry this weekend.
Your rent is overdue, and the landlady is losing patience.

hints: Employers notice who shows up reliably.
Managers are picked from their own staff. Shifts at another workplace don't count for that.
Long work weeks pile up stress. Past a point you wear out: rest, sauna or a lighter week helps.
A well-rested mind learns faster. So does a well-read one.
Better clothes open more doors than you would think.
Money in your pocket attracts the wrong kind of attention.
Nobody stays happy without a little sauna now and then.
Living with your parents is cheap, but it wears on you.
The city pays well, if you have the papers for it.
Stay too long in one job and someone upstairs may notice you.
Prices go up and down with the times. So do wages.
Never skip meals. A hungry week is a wasted week.
Old-timers say the furniture factory always needs strong hands.
A summer without a dance at the lava is a summer wasted.
Everyone ends up at the Trokari sooner or later. Even me.
Nobody can cram a whole course into one week. Plan for the long haul.
Appliances lose value the day you carry them home. Land and houses hold theirs.
The best jobs in the village have only one desk. Somebody else may get there first.
Happiness fades a little every week, and the happier you are, the faster it fades.
Money in the bank is safe from pickpockets, and it grows a little.
An evening with Pekki makes anyone's life look good by comparison.
Matti says a coffee break is the best medicine for a hard week. Matti is usually right.
Olli is insufferable, but you'll learn more from him than from any book.
Never split a bill with Juho. But do let him look at your savings.
Pellinen's door is always open. The curtains, never.
